main_body: Tall dark stone throne with a high backrest, a red cushion seat with a gold front trim, and a dark base plinth
top_band: x=8: rows 18-19 dark red (L=61) directly followed by pink rows 20-21 (L=106, 152) and a cream/gold edge at row 22 (L=208). This reads as one face-on cushion gradient, not a separate lighter top surface.
evidence: The seat is the key surface and it is drawn as a face-on cushion. The dark red top rows 18-19 grade straight into lighter pink front rows 20-21 and a cream trim line at row 22, so no clear lighter top band is separated from the front. At most about 2 rows could be the seat top, which is the thin-seat failure in the guide. The backrest and the dark body below (rows 23-27) are flat front-facing panels with no visible horizontal surfaces, and the plinth is a plain front strip. No eave shadow or inset is drawn. The whole throne is a front elevation.

style.evidence: The red cushion has a decent 4-5 step ramp, but the stone is only a few near-neutral dark greys (#131317, #1e1e24, #2a2a32) with almost no grain, and large areas of the backrest and body are nearly the same dark value. Edge pixels are 96% near-neutral, so the outline is a neutral black sticker line, whereas the references use tinted material outlines (1% and 33% neutral). The candidate has 18 distinct colours against 38-40 in the references. Its median of 16 colours per tile is close to the references (17 and 20), but that figure comes mostly from the small cushion and trim areas. Stone shading is shallower and more sticker-like than the references.
